static_traits.name: Zhang Min
static_traits.social_status: Tense relationships with colleagues; a few friends to talk with, but work-related worries not yet shared with them
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; never experienced similar psychological problems; not yet received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, cooperative in exploration, but skeptical with marked self-denial

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling not competent enough at work, with recurring thoughts of 'I will never be promoted'; it all started with a negligence-caused vegetable write-off loss about six months ago.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling now because these thoughts are affecting my self-esteem and job satisfaction.
growth_experiences: About six months ago, while working at a grocery store, the client caused a batch of vegetables to be written off due to negligence. Although the employer did not blame her on the spot or explicitly express negative evaluation, the incident lingered in her mind. Since then, she keeps replaying this mistake, believing it seriously blocked her promotion chances; whenever promotion news or discussion arises, she automatically associates it with the mistake and thinks 'they will not consider me'. Under its influence, she began working twice as hard, extra diligent to 'make up' for the error, while her relationships with colleagues grew tense from her anxiety and self-doubt, gradually reducing communication with them. She has not yet shared these worries with friends; she lost interest in previously enjoyed activities, with markedly lowered self-esteem and work satisfaction.

core_beliefs: I am not competent enough (not good enough)

special_situations.event: Six months ago at work, negligence caused a batch of vegetables to be written off
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make one obvious mistake, I will permanently destroy my promotion opportunity
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Works overtime and more diligently to 'make up' for mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I ruined all my promotion chances

special_situations.event: Announcements or discussions of promotion opportunities at the company
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not perfectly without fault, I cannot be promoted
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: When promotion approaches, pressures oneself and overworks to seek 'perfect performance'

special_situations.event: The employer did not explicitly blame or address the mistake at the time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Without explicit approval or explanation, it means they have lost trust in me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing communication with management to avoid being noticed or evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They have already lost confidence in me

special_situations.event: Daily interaction and collaboration with colleagues
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If colleagues think something is wrong with me, it means I am truly unqualified
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding conversations with colleagues, reduced social contact
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They may think something is wrong with me

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and promoted, to gain others' trust and affirmation
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being negated, seen as incompetent, worried one mistake leads to lasting shame and rejection
defense_goal: Through excessive diligence and self-criticism, maintains a sense of value and avoids negative external evaluations
Keeping distance and reducing communication to lower the risk of criticism or exposing inadequacy again

object_relations.self_representation: An employee not competent enough, prone to mistakes and needing constant compensation
object_relations.object_representation: A calm but potentially harsh judge (superior / colleagues) who may negate her at any time

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes a behavioral experiment to test his belief about promotion
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously treating 'damage is irreversible' as a valid premise, believing counseling can hardly change reality (a pessimistic preset about change)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expressing concerns in a polite but skeptical tone (like 'I am not sure this can change anything'), steady pace, maintaining basic cooperation but emphasizing her own concerns.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor probes for concrete evidence about 'others losing trust' and conducts a fact check
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributing inner self-denial and worries of not being recognized to others, believing others are already disappointed in her (transference: projecting inner unease onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Insisting on subjective judgments of others' negative views, using vague wording (like 'they must remember my mistake'), avoiding detailed evidence, while maintaining basic communication.

manifestations: Living alone and not yet sharing work-related worries with friends
Reduces communication with colleagues; relationships grow strained
Losing interest in previously enjoyed activities

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeatedly reproaching herself 'I am not good enough'
Excessive self-scrutiny and pressure when promotion opportunities arise
Reducing communication for fear of others' judgment

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Believing my superior has lost trust in me, despite lacking clear evidence
Feeling colleagues 'may think I have a problem' and reducing contact because of it

positive_force: Willing to try behavioral experiments, with some willingness to cooperate
Keeps working hard and diligently at work to improve performance
Has some social support (several friends to talk to)
negative_force: Cognitive distortions like overgeneralization and predicting the future reinforcing self-denial
Self-worth excessively dependent on external evaluation (like promotion)
Avoiding interaction with colleagues leads to decreased support and relationship tension
Impaired self-esteem, decreased interest affecting career engagement

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding communication with colleagues (reduced social interaction)
antecedent: Recalling a mistake six months ago at work
When the company announces or discusses promotion opportunities
Feeling that others may be evaluating oneself
target_behavior.core_reason: Seeing one mistake as a total negation of her ability, and projecting inner self-doubt as others' view of 'not trusting me / thinking something is wrong with me', leading to avoiding communication
target_behavior.function: Escaping negative evaluation and possible shame, briefly relieving anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Tense relationships with colleagues, weakened social support, further intensifying isolation and anxiety

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive diligence and self-pressure (working overtime to 'make up for' mistakes)
antecedent: When promotion opportunities or performance reviews arise
target_behavior.core_reason: Using the conditional assumption 'must be perfect without fault to be recognized' to undo the core belief 'I am not competent enough', thereby seeking security and worth through overwork
target_behavior.function: Trying to gain recognition and lower the risk of being negated
target_behavior.consequence: Ongoing pressure and exhaustion, decline in job satisfaction, possibly further reinforcing self-doubt
